title: Hugh McGary, the Blue Licks Hothead
summary: Irish-born Hugh McGary (1744–1806) came into Kentucky in 1775 with Boone's party, settled near Fort Harrod, and built McGary's Station around 1779 at Shawnee Springs in today's…
bodyMarkdown:
Irish-born Hugh McGary (1744–1806) came into Kentucky in 1775 with Boone's party, settled near Fort Harrod, and built McGary's Station around 1779 at Shawnee Springs in today's Mercer County. On August 19, 1782, as a major under Col. John Todd, he commanded the center at Blue Licks.

Boone urged caution at the Licking ford, but the militia crossed and walked into an ambush. A later tradition says McGary led the way shouting for anyone who wasn't a coward to follow; it comes from recollections gathered decades afterward and is not in Boone's own 1782 or 1784 accounts. In the rout, roughly seventy Kentuckians fell in minutes, including Todd and Israel Boone. McGary survived—and later killed the surrendered Shawnee chief Moluntha on Logan's 1786 Ohio raid, earning a court-martial suspension. He is remembered as Kentucky's classic frontier hothead, a reputation built partly on that tradition.
Sources: [Boone to Gov. Harrison, Aug. 30, 1782](https://kynghistory.ky.gov/Our-History/History-of-the-Guard/Pages/The-Battle-of-Blue-Licks.aspx) · [ExploreKYHistory](https://explorekyhistory.ky.gov/items/show/590) · [Battle of Blue Licks](/stories/battle-of-blue-licks/)
